27. It is not clear to the Committee if complaints forwarded to CVO/CBI are treated
as disposed off by CVC. The Committee is of the view that CVC should continue
monitoring of such complaints particularly if these fall within its jurisdiction, till these
have been finally investigated.  (Para 4.11)
28. The Committee takes note of the penalties sanctioned by the CVC. (Para 4.13)
Chief Vigilance Officers
29. The Committee takes note of the high number of pending cases with the CVOs.
The Committee feels disciplinary proceedings should be concluded in a time-bound
manner preferably within a year of issuance of charge-sheet and all cases of disciplinary
proceedings extending beyond the period so stipulated should be closely monitored to
ensure quick finalization of such cases. (Para 4.15)
30. The Committee feels that a full time CVOs should be appointed in all sensitive
Central Ministries/ Departments and the bodies/PSUs falling within their purview. This
appointee should be from outside the organization having adequate experience in dealing
with vigilance cases. This would ensure transparency and impartiality in the conduct of
vigilance proceedings. (Para 4.17)
41

42
Chief Technical Examiner’s Organisation
31. The Committee commends the work of the CTEO which helped in the saving of
resources and recommends that avenues may be explored on how the CTEO can be
provided with the desired manpower as soon as possible. The nature of graft and
corruption is becoming highway complex and appropriate analysis can only be carried out
with the help of professionals with experience and expertise in the area. The DoPT must
look into the matter expeditiously and ensure that the organization is well staffed.
Sufficient Budgetary allocations should be made to ensure that the organization can
attract the right personnel and is able to create required support infrastructure to
investigate complaints. The organization may also explore the possibility of taking
professionals on deputations or on contract. (Para 4.20 )
Departmental Enquiries against CBI officials
32. The Committee takes serious view of the matter. The cases against erring CBI
officials must be fast-tracked and disposed off as early as possible. Emphasis must be
laid on cases which are pending for more than two years. The CVC must ensure that
departmental proceedings in all such cases are expeditiously completed. (Para 4.22)
New Initiatives Proposed by the Commission
33. The Committee takes note of the new initiatives and appreciates the efforts of the
Commission in improving preventive vigilance in organizations. The Committee believes
that preventive vigilance must be a priority area for the Commission which is likely to have
positive impact on the performance index of the organization. (Para 4.24)
Central Administrative Tribunal
34. The Committee has taken note of the vacancy position and notes the efforts
made for filling up vacancies. It also notes that the disposal rate of the Tribunal is
lower than rate of institution of cases thereby leading to increased pendency. Tribunals
are meant for providing speedy and inexpensive justice to the public servants. The high
pendency runs contrary to the legislative intent of the CAT Act, 1985. The Committee
recommends that the Tribunal must take steps to reduce pendency. Vacancies in
Tribunal are also responsible for this state of pendency in Tribunal and therefore the
Committee recommends that the Department should make every possible effort to
expeditiously fill the vacant posts in the Tribunal. (Para 4.28)
35. The Committee further notes that the Tribunal system was originally envisaged
as an alternative in order to reduce the burden on the courts. The Committee desires
that the Tribunal should undertake a study in order to determine the percentage of
cases in which appeal has been filed in the High Courts in last five years and examine
if steps can be taken to reduce appeals to High Courts. (Para 4.29)
Status of Infrastructure and Initiatives taken bv the Tribunal to Improve Efficiencv
36. The Committee while taking note of the above initiatives, is of the view that
computerization of various Benches of CAT must be completed as soon as possible and
cases pending for over three years taken on priority basis and disposed off at the
earliest. The Committee recommends that adequate financial resources must be made
available to the CAT Benches so that the computerization and other initiatives taken by
it do not suffer for want of adequate funds. (Para 4.33)

43
Central Information Commission
Submission of RTI Returns
37. The Committee takes serious note of tendency to evade filing of returns by public
authorities to the Commission. The Department should ensure 100% compliance with all
statutory regulations of the RTI Act including Section 25 (2) which mandates filing
Annual Returns by Public Authorities. (Para 4.38)
38. The  DoPT must take up the matter with all Ministries/Departments and ensure
that all public authorities file returns with CVC as mandated by the RTI Act. There can
be no justification for flouting the rules by Government Departments. The Committee
is pained to find Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions in the top ten
lists of Defaulters. The Ministry is the nodal Ministry with respect to implementation
of the RTI Act and therefore must lead by example. (Para 4.39)
39. The direction given by DoPT in their guidelines for implementation of Section 4 of
the RTI Act which required appointment of a Joint Secretary rank officer as the Nodal
Officer should be followed in letter and spirit. The Committee feels that all Ministries/
Departments/Organisations themselves must encourage suo-motu disclosure of relevant
information. The Committee suggests the publishing of RTI requests and their replies on
the websites of the Departments so that duplicity of requests is avoided. All Departments
must make an analysis of information which is sought most often from applicants and
provide it on their website as suo-motu disclosure. (Para 4.40)
Disposal of Cases bv the Commission
40. The Committee takes serious note of the increased pendency with the
Commission as its rate of disposal is lower than the rate of institution of cases. The
Commission was set up with a mandate to provide speedy relief to the aggrieved parties.
However, the current situation runs counter to this mandate. (Para 4.43)
Vacancies in the Commission
41. The Committee is not happy with the non-filling up of vacancies in the
Commission. The Committee desires that the DoPT should fill these vacant positions
without any further delay. The vacancies are to a large extent, responsible for the
increasing pendency of cases in the Commission. (Para 4.45)
Plan Schemes of the Commission
42. The Committee is happy to note that the CIC shall have its own building in the
near future and requisite infrastructure to function smoothly. The Committee is happy
to find that the Commission is fully utilizing allocation made for construction of its
building. The Committee also appreciates the e-Governance initiative of the Commission
and hopes that the system will further strengthen working of the Commission and cut
down delays in disposal of appeals/complaints. (Para 4.49)
Union Public Service Commission
Civil Services Examination
43. The Committee takes note of the initiative taken by UPSC to ensure smooth
conduct of the Civil Services examination. The Committee has, however, noticed that

44
the time taken to evaluate the answer scripts of the Civil Services (Main) Examination
has not reduced and there is often a lot of uncertainty surrounding the date of
declaration of the results of the Main examination. The Commission must make efforts
to reduce the time taken for evaluation of answer books of Main examination so that
the recruitment process could be completed in a shorter time span. (Para 4.51)
44. The Committee desires that the UPSC should examine whether details with respect
to moderation of marks can be put in the public domain without compromising the
objective behind it so that the fairness of the UPSC is not questioned and also the
desired level of transparency prevails. (Para 4.53)
Recruitment in Other Organisations
45. The Committee appreciates the Constitutional mandate of the UPSC. However, it
feels that a system for recruitment needs to be made faster and less time consuming.
The Commission may work with DoPT to evolve a suitable system for faster recruitment
to posts in these organizations. (Para 4.55)
Initiatives Taken by the UPSC
46. The Committee takes note of the initiatives of the Commission and feels that
the wider application of Information Technology in the examination process must be
carried out only after studying its implications on the students from rural/tribal
backgrounds. It should be ensured that candidates from far flung rural and tribal areas
are not put to in any disadvantageous position in recruitment examinations conducted by
the Commission. (Para 4.57)
Staff Selection Commission
Conduct of Examinations
47. The Committee takes note of the fact that the number of candidates applying
each year for the various examinations has increased considerably and the Commission
is doing a commendable job in conducting these exams in a fair and transparent
manner. (Para 4.61)
48. The Committee feels that the time frames as stated by the Commission needs to
be further reduced as most of the examinations conducted by the Commission are of an
objective nature, there is scope for reducing the time taken for declaration of results.
The Commission must seriously consider the use of an online exam for the conduct of
these exams so that the time taken for of these exams gets reduced. However, while
conducting such examinations, it should be ensured that the candidates from rural
areas/ economically weaker sections (EWS) are not put to any disadvantage in such
online exams. (Para 4.63)
49. The Committee also desires that the Commission should consider conducting the
exams online on multiple dates. In this regard, the examination process of the GMAT
exam may be studied carefully and its applicability in the examinations conducted by the
Commission evaluated. Similarly, the pattern of online examinations conducted by
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) may also be considered. (Para 4.64)
Statutory/Status
50. The Committee supports above recommendation of the Expert Group. The DoPT may
pursue the matter and ensure that statutory backing is provided to the SSC. The
Committee further desires that the DoPT may look into the other recommendations of the
Expert Group and ensure that they are implemented as far as practical. (Para 4.66)

INTRODUCTION
I, Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public
Grievances, Law and Justice, having been authorised by the Committee on its behalf, do hereby present the
Seventy-Seventh Report on the Lokpal and Lokayuktas and Other Related Law (Amendment) Bill, 2014.
2. In pursuance of the Rules relating to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees,
the Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha referred the Lokpal and Lokayuktas and Other Related Law (Amendment)
Bill, 2014 (Annexure-I), as introduced in the Lok Sabha on the 18th December, 2014 to the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice on the 25th
December, 2014, for examination and report to Parliament within three months i.e. by the 24th March,
2015. In order to solicit the views of stakeholders, the Committee issued a Press Communiqué on 7th
January, 2015. In response thereto the Committee received several memoranda containing suggestions from
various organizations/individuals/experts. Comments of the Department of Personnel and Training on the
views/suggestions so received, were placed for the consideration of the Committee.
3. The Committee heard the views of Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training, Ministry of
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions and Director, Central Bureau of Investigation during its meeting
held on 8th January, 2015. The Committee then heard the views of Secretary, Central Vigilance Commission
and Director of Prosecution of Central Bureau of Investigation during the meeting held on 3rd March, 2015.
4. The Committee heard the views of Shri Ashok Kapur, Director, Institute of Directors; Professor, K
Elumalai, Director, School of Law, Indira Gandhi National Open University;  Smt. Anjali Bhardwaj and Shri
Nikhil Dey of National Campaign for Peoples' Right to Information and Ms. Guninder Gill during its meeting
held on the 15th April, 2015. The Committee also heard Dr. Jayaprakash Narayan, General Secretary, Lok
Satta on 26th May, 2015.
5. The Committee again heard the Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training and Director,
Central Bureau of Investigation; Chairperson, Central Board of Direct Taxes; Secretary, Central Vigilance
Commission and Director, Enforcement Directorate on 16th July, 2015.
6. The Committee wrote to all the recognised National and State Political Parties to hear their views on
the Bill and particularly on Clause 6. The Committee received written views from Bharatiya Janata Party,
Communist Party of India, Shiromani Akali Dal, YSR Congress Party, All India Trinamool Congress, All
India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, Indian National Lok Dal and Aam Aadmi Party. All India Anna
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, All India Trinamool Congress and Indian National Lok Dal presented their
views on the Bill during its sittings held on 14th October and 16th November, 2015.
7. The Committee also heard the views of Indian Revenue Service Association, Indian Civil Accounts
Service Association, Confederation of Central Government Gazetted Officers' Organisations and Confederation
of Civil Service Association during the meeting held on 14th October, 2015. It has received written views of
Central Secretariat Non-gazetted Employees Union, Central Secretariat Service Group A Officers Association
and Central Secretariat (Promotee) Assistants' Association.
(v)

Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 was enacted to setup an independent and empowered anti-
corruption institution, namely, Lokpal at union level and for making enabling provision for
establishment of Lokayukta for States for prompt inquiry and investigation into allegation of
corruption by public functionaries and to fulfil the obligations of our country under the United
Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC). The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 came into
force w.e.f. 16th January, 2014. Pursuant thereto the Union Government framed and notified the
following Rules thereunder to implement the provisions of the said Act:-
(i) The search Committee (Constitution, Terms and Conditions of Appointment of
Members and the Manner of Selection of Panels of Names for Appointment of
Chairperson and Members of Lokpal) Rules, 2014; and
(ii) The Public Servants (Furnishing of Information and Annual Returns of Assets and
Liabilities and Limit for Exemption of Assets in Filing Returns) Rules, 2014

changes, amendments to the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 have been proposed under the
Lokpal and Lokayuktas and Other Related Law (Amendment) Bill, 2014 (Annexure-I) .

Leader of Single Largest Opposition Party to be Part of Selection Committee in the Absence
of Leader of Opposition (LoP) in Lok Sabha
3.0. Clause 2 inter alia  seeks to amend Section 4 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
allowing the leader of the single largest opposition party in the House of People (Lok Sabha) to
be part of the Selection Committee for Lokpal when there is no recognized Leader of Opposition
(LoP) in that House.
3.1. The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) has stated that the amendment is
necessitated keeping in view the political exigencies which emerged after the Sixteenth General
Election to Lok Sabha as there is no Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha in the current Lok Sabha.
Similar amendment was made to Section 4A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act,
1946 in November, 2014 enabling leader of largest opposition party to be part of the selection
process for appointment of a new Director of CBI. Similar provisions also exist for the
appointment of Chief Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) under Section 4 of CVC Act, 2003.
3.2. Several Members of the Committee raised questions regarding a situation wherein two or
more parties have the same strength in the House of People and wondered, in that situation, who
would become a part of the Selection Committee for Lokpal. In response thereto, the DoPT has
submitted that such a situation is a rare one. In such a situation, the selection of Lokpal can either
be made by treating the position of Leader of Opposition (LoP) as vacant and proceeding with
making the selection or to wait for the decision of the Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha to recognise
the leader of one party as per the provisions of the Salary and Allowances of Leader of Opposition
in Parliament Act, 1977. The Explanation to Section 2 of the Salary and Allowances of Leaders of
Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977 permits the Presiding Officer of the House (Lok Sabha/Rajya
Sabha) to recognize the leader of one political party in opposition to the Government as Leader of
Opposition when there are two or more parties having similar numerical strength in that House.
3.3. Most of the non-official witnesses who appeared before the Committee also agreed with the
amendment.
Recommendations/Observations of the Committee
3.4. The Committee notes that in the present Lok Sabha, there is no recognized Leader
of Opposition and such a situation can arise in future as well. In the absence of Leader of
Opposition it is not possible to constitute the Selection Committee of Lok Pal as per
provisions of the Lok Pal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. In order to overcome such a situation,
amendment is proposed to provide that the Leader of Opposition recognised as such in the
Lok Sabha or where there is no such Leader of Opposition, the leader of the single largest
